bg_facts: Two critical flaws were found in PHP.
PHP helps run about 70% of websites.

slides.title: What *happened*
slides.body: Security firm Wiz, working with AI models, found two critical flaws in PHP, the language behind about 70% of websites. Fixes came out on Oct 21.

slides.title: Why it is *serious*
slides.body: The bugs let an attacker run code on a server without logging in. Both scored 9.2 out of 10, and they go back to PHP 5.4.

slides.title: AI did *the hard part*
slides.body: Wiz says AI models helped find the bugs and build working attacks, a chain of steps at the edge of what human researchers could do by hand.

slides.title: The *race*
slides.body: Cloudflare saw tens of thousands of attack attempts in the first 45 minutes, and millions after. Government sites in the UK, Finland and France went offline while teams patched.

slides.title: What to *do*
slides.body: Run a website? Ask your host or developer if PHP is on 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. A WordPress update alone does not fix it.

cta.small: Follow @autopilot.oi for the AI stories that matter, explained in plain words.
